obligation: Bank recall of a misdirected wire (funds response)
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.211 (UCC Article 4A cancellation and amendment of payment orders); FBI IC3 PSA I-091124-PSA
trigger: A wire was sent on fraudulent instructions: a buyer wire (BEC variant A), a title trust disbursement (variant B), or a sales escrow refund, owner payout, or agent payout (variant C)
deadline: Immediately on discovery; target within 1 hour (POL-03 4.4). After the receiving bank accepts the payment order, cancellation needs that bank's agreement, so minutes matter
notify: The sending bank's wire room or fraud desk (request a recall and hold); in variant A the buyer calls their own bank and the company alerts its bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational, not a notification duty
clock_starts: When anyone learns the funds went to a wrong account
owner: President, Title and Closing (variant B); Controller (variant C); closer coaches the buyer (variant A)

obligation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) complaint
trigger: Any BEC attempt with a loss, or any attempt involving a trust or escrow account
deadline: As soon as possible, regardless of the amount (voluntary; no legal deadline). The FBI states IC3 may help banks and law enforcement freeze funds
notify: IC3 at www.ic3.gov with full banking details; the buyer files their own complaint in variant A
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information of Title and Closing without authorization, involving at least 500 consumers. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise; information is unencrypted if the key was accessed
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov, with the six items in 314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi): institution name and contact, information types, date or date range, number of consumers, general description, and any law enforcement delay determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Title and Closing is a financial institution with customer information on about 98,000 consumers (P03 section 1.1). A single agent mailbox usually holds fewer than 500, so count and document; a ransomware theft of closing files would exceed it
clock_starts: Discovery: the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent, other than the person committing the breach (314.4(j)(2)); contractor agents count

obligation: FTC notice: law enforcement delay of public disclosure
trigger: A law enforcement official determines in writing that notifying the public would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still filed on time. The official may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: State the determination and the official's contact details in the FTC notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of electronic data containing personal information of Florida residents (for example name with Social Security, driver license, or financial account number with access code; or a username or email address with a password)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email to the address in the company's records (never through a compromised mailbox); content per 501.171(4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - both entities are covered entities. The FTC rule has no individual-notice procedure, so the federal-regulator deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) does not apply; confirm with counsel
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida notice not required after a no-harm determination
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the written determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for a mailbox with no Social Security, ID, or account access data; counsel decides

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay of individual notice
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation and asks in writing
deadline: Individual notice is delayed for the period stated in the agency's written request (which the agency may revoke or extend in writing)
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request in the decision log
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination. A 15-day extension, if good cause is given in writing within the 30 days, applies only to the notice to individuals, never to this notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs: synopsis, number of Floridians affected, free services offered, copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Service provider breach notice to the company (inbound)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a); contract terms under 16 CFR 314.4(f)(2) and STD-03
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the title production vendor, transaction platform vendor, screening provider, or MSSP) has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: The third-party agent must notify the company as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after its determination; STD-03 contracts require 5 business days for Tier 1
notify: The company (Security Manager and General Counsel); the company then gives the notices in 501.171(3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts (P03 G-032; POAM-015)
clock_starts: Third-party agent's determination of the breach

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: Breach notification statutes of each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Affected people who live outside Florida (about 25% of buyers; out-of-state property owners and tenants)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and, where the state requires it, the state attorney general, regulators, or consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check the state of residence of every affected person; apply each state's law

obligation: Florida Real Estate Commission notice of an escrow dispute
trigger: A diverted or missing earnest money deposit leads to conflicting demands on funds in the sales escrow account, or the broker has a good-faith doubt about who is entitled to them
deadline: Written notice to the Commission within 15 business days after the last demand or after the doubt arises; institute a settlement procedure within 30 business days
notify: Florida Real Estate Commission (by the Broker of Record)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the brokerage holds the deposit and demands conflict (variant C)
clock_starts: Last party's demand or start of good-faith doubt

obligation: Title insurance underwriter notice
citation: Title agency agreement and closing protection letter terms (contract)
trigger: Loss or suspected loss of funds from a title escrow trust account, or a claim by a buyer, seller, or lender
deadline: Per the agency agreement; treat as same day
notify: Underwriter agency or claims contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
clock_starts: Discovery of the loss or claim

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
citation: Cyber insurance policy ($10 million limit; $1 million funds transfer fraud sublimit) (contract)
trigger: Suspected security incident, funds transfer fraud, or extortion
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging any incident vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline; the carrier assigns panel breach counsel and forensics
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Lender client and homebuilder notice
citation: Closing services agreements with the 2 regional lenders and the national homebuilder (contract)
trigger: Security incident affecting their borrowers' or buyers' information or funds handled by Title and Closing
deadline: Per each agreement (counsel checks the contract register)
notify: Each client's designated security or legal contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the ransomware runbook; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties
owner: Chief Executive Officer with General Counsel

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; voluntary reporting to CISA is encouraged. Recheck when final
clock_starts: n/a until a final rule is effective

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: Within four business days after determining materiality
notify: SEC and investors
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held (N53-R05); private equity sponsor informed by the CEO under the shareholder agreement

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in federal contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in federal contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
